title: Modeling Ovarian Cancer Multicellular Spheroid Behavior in a Dynamic 3D Peritoneal Microdevice
protocol: Design the microfluidic channel pattern using CAD software.
Send the CAD drawing to a photomask company to produce the photomask.
Wash the silicon wafer with ultrasonication in acetone, isopropanol, and deionized water for 15 minutes each.
Dry the wafer with pressurized nitrogen gas.
Heat the silicon wafer on a hot plate at 250 °C for 15 min to completely dry it.
Spin-coat a layer of SU-8 2075 photoresist (125 µm-thick) onto the silicon wafer at 1,800 rpm.
Bake the photoresist-coated wafer on a hot plate at 65 °C for 5 min and then at 95 °C for 25 min.
Spin-coat another layer of SU-8 2075 photoresist to obtain a final thickness of 250 µm.
Bake the photoresist-coated wafer on a hot plate at 65 °C for 7 min and then at 95 °C for 30 min.
Slowly cool the wafer to room temperature.
Align the photomask directly on top of the wafer.
Expose the wafer to UV light for 20 seconds to crosslink the pattern.
Bake the wafer with photoresist at 65°C for 5 minutes.
Bake the wafer with photoresist at 95°C for 12 minutes.
Cool the wafer to room temperature.
Immerse the wafer in SU-8 developer for 25 minutes.
Rinse the wafer with isopropanol.
Dry the wafer with pressured air.
If a milky solution is observed during rinsing, immerse the wafer back into SU-8 developer for additional time.
Place the wafer on a hot plate at 180°C for 10 minutes to heal any potential cracks.
Turn off the hot plate and slowly cool down the wafer to room temperature by leaving it on the hot plate.
Add a few drops of trichloro (1H, 1H, 2H, 2H-perfluorooctyl) silane in a vial cap.
Put the vial cap in the vacuum desiccator.
Place the wafer next to the vial cap to silanize for 10 minutes.
Wrap the wafer with aluminum foil to create a holder.
Mix the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) base and curing agent at a 10:1 mass ratio using a centrifugal mixer under mixing and degas function.
Pour the PDMS mixture slowly onto the wafer to a height of around 5 mm.
Degas the PDMS under vacuum for 40 minutes.
Cure the PDMS in an oven at 65°C for 2 hours.
Peel the PDMS slab off the master.
Trim the PDMS along the channels until it matches the size of a glass slide.
Punch the PDMS with a 1-mm biopsy punch to create inlets and outlets.
Clean the PDMS surface with pressurized air and adhesive tape.
Place the PDMS slab into a plasma cleaner with the channel side facing upwards.
Place a clean glass slide into the plasma cleaner alongside the PDMS slab.
Treat the PDMS and glass slide under air plasma at high RF level for 1 min.
Bind the PDMS to the glass slide to create an irreversible covalent bond.
Place the PDMS chip on a hot plate at 150 °C for 1 h.
Sterilize the microfluidic channel with 30 µL of 75% ethanol.
Remove the ethanol and rinse twice with 30 µL of sterilized phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Thoroughly aspirate PBS in the channels.
Prepare a 10 µg/mL fibronectin solution in serum-free M199:MCDB105 (1:1) medium.
Pipette the fibronectin solution up and down, with special care to avoid bubble formation.
Slowly fill up each channel with 30 µL of fibronectin solution.
Seal the channels with tape and incubate the chip overnight at 4 °C.
Culture HPMCs in 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) culture medium under 5% CO2 at 37 °C until 80% confluence.
Rinse the HPMCs with 3 mL of PBS.
Trypsinize HPMCs with 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin/0.01% EDTA (TE) solution for 30 s.
Neutralize with 4 mL of 10% FBS culture medium and spin down the cells at 1,000 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend the HPMCs in 2 mL of 10% FBS culture medium.
Count the cell number with a hemocytometer and adjust the cell concentration to 3.5×106/mL.
Warm the fibronectin-coated microfluidic chip in a 37 °C incubator for 5 min before use.
Completely aspirate the fibronectin solution.
Slowly pipette 30 µL of HPMC suspension into each channel.
Seal the channels with tape and place the devices in the CO2 incubator overnight.
Dissolve 0.5% agarose in sterilized water by boiling.
Dispense 50 μL of agarose solution into each well of 96-well plates.
Leave the plates in the hood for 20 min to allow the agarose to solidify.
Rinse SKOV-3 cells with 3 mL of PBS.
Trypsinize SKOV-3 cells with 2 mL of TE solution for 3 min.
Neutralize trypsinized cells with 4 mL of 5% FBS culture medium and spin down the cells at 1,000 x g for 5 min.
Count SKOV-3 cell number with a hemocytometer.
Resuspend cells in 5% FBS culture medium at a density of 5,000 cells/mL.
Transfer 200 μL of cell suspension into each agarose-coated well.
Culture the wells under 5% CO2 at 37 °C for 48 h.
Transfer cancer spheroids to a 50-mL centrifuge tube pre-wetted with 1 mL of serum-free medium and spin down at 750 x g for 5 min.
Prepare 2.5 µg/mL of 5-chloromethylfluorescein diacetate (CMFDA) solution in serum-free M199:MCDB105 medium.
Resuspend cancer spheroids in 1 mL of CMFDA solution and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Centrifuge the spheroids at 750 x g for 5 min.
Rinse cancer spheroids with 2 mL of serum-free medium and centrifuge at 750 x g for 5 min.
Repeat rinsing step twice to remove remaining fluorescent dye from the medium.
Resuspend cancer spheroids in serum-free M199:MCDB105 medium.
Count the spheroid number with a hemocytometer.
Adjust the concentration to 2,000 spheroids/mL with serum-free medium.
Slowly inject 100 μL of serum-free M199:MCDB105 medium to wash away non-adhered mesothelial cells inside the channels.
Load 30 μL of fluorescent-labeled spheroid suspension into each channel.
Place the microfluidic chip into the CO2 incubator.
Attach a syringe loaded with fresh, serum-free M199:MCDB105 medium to a 1 m-long tube.
Place the syringe on the syringe pump and secure the plunger and body of the syringe.
Install the syringe pump in a horizontal position at the same height as the microfluidic chip inside the incubator.
Quickly infuse the whole tube with medium by pressing and holding the fast forward button until the medium overflows the tubing.
Run the injection at the desired flow rate.
Connect the tubing to the inlet of the channel.
Place excess inlet tubing in the incubator to warm the medium before injection into the channels.
Choose appropriate connectors to facilitate connection between the tubing and the channel.
Avoid introducing any bubbles into the syringe, tubing, and connections.
Connect the outlet of the channel to a 50-mL conical tube using a short output tube to collect outflow medium.
Observe HPMCs and cancer spheroids with a bright-field or fluorescence microscope after 1 hour of perfusion.
Take pictures of the observed cells and spheroids.
